correctness.rationale: The separate finite check /workspace/branches/5e1de70f-c72b-48ff-9568-89b779f2d952/independent_check.py reconstructed KG(5,2), enumerated all ten-vertex spanning paths modulo reversal, and checked both-end rotations and BFS from every state. It obtained 120 paths (four for each of 30 nonedge endpoint pairs), 240 edges, degree four, and shells (1,4,11,25,39,29,11) at every state. The action preserves rotations. An element stabilizing the reference path cannot reverse it, since 01 and 24 are disjoint but their reversed images 14 and 04 are not; fixing the path pointwise fixes every two-subset and hence is the identity. The computed four reference neighbors give exactly the stated inverse pair, double transposition and transposition, with right multiplication as claimed; conjugates of (0 3) by (0 3 2 4) generate S_4 on its support, and (0 1)(2 3) then generates the missing transposition with 1. Full breadth-first enumeration gives eccentricity six. The edge-exchange criterion also follows: no old endpoints are adjacent in the non-Hamiltonian Petersen graph, so a one-edge addition must join an endpoint to an interior vertex; to undo the cycle and the degree-three vertex requires deleting the interior vertex's edge toward that endpoint. No frozen script was executed for the independent check.

A natural non-Hamiltonian cubic test case lies outside the spanning-square connectivity theorem; identifying its reconfiguration graph with a specific S5 Cayley graph explains uniformity across all states and supplies exact answers for the reachability distance between configurations. The complete reference-path metric is a useful invariant of this specific move graph, not an arbitrary cutoff.
